headline: Asia: Russian attacks kill 17 in Ukraine after Trump strikes diesel deal with Putin
script:
Good morning. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- Asia: Russian attacks kill 17 in Ukraine after Trump strikes diesel deal with Putin.
- South Asia: Trump sows doubt on plan to livestream US military execution.
- Western Russia: Zelenskyy: Russia thanked US for easing sanctions by bombing Zaporizhzhia.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Pentagon, Raytheon sign $6.3B deal to replenish US missile interceptor supply.
- Military Times, 18 hours ago: Pentagon, Raytheon sign $6.3B deal to replenish US missile interceptor supply.
The contract "supports urgent replenishment of missile defense inventory that has been successfully used in combat," Raytheon said.
- Military Times, 20 hours ago: Soldiers intervene on roadside to save children from alleged knife attack.
Three soldiers sprang into action when a highway crash in Washington turned into a knife attack on two children.
The Caribbean - bottom line: StJMC mulls action against companies for hanging wires.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 9 hours ago: StJMC mulls action against companies for hanging wires.
WESTERN BUREAU: The St James Municipal Corporation is calling on telecommunications companies with low-hanging wires, which were displaced by Hurricane Melissa a year ago, to address them immediately or risk legal action in the interest of the public safety. Montego Bay Mayor Richard Vernon issued the warning on Thursday at the St James Municipal Corporation’s (StJMC) City Hall 2026 Municipal Budget Presentation at the Montego Bay Cultural Centre, where he outlined plans for the corporation’s $2.8-billion budget expenditure for the 2027-2028 financial year.

President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says Russia responded to the easing of US sanctions with deadly strikes on Zaporizhzhia, where 12 people have been killed.
- Ukrainska Pravda, one hour ago: Zelenskyy after speaking with Macron: threat of missile strikes remains particularly high in coming days.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has discussed the challenges posed by the easing of US sanctions on Russian oil products with French President Emmanuel Macron.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 3 hours ago: Russians hit restaurant building in Kyiv during missile attack, leaving 6 injured.
Debris from a drone reportedly fell on a 25-storey residential building and an eight-storey office building in Kyiv's Solomianskyi district, and later a restaurant was hit during a missile strike.
- Ukrainska Pravda, one hour ago: Ukraine strikes Samara oil facility again, Russian command posts and electronic warfare station also hit.
Ukraine's defence forces struck the Samara linear production dispatching station in Russia's Samara Oblast, along with Russian command posts and an electronic warfare station on the night of 9-10 October.
Southern Europe: no notable developments in the last 24 hours.

A rare pair of waterspouts swept ashore in western Sicily on Friday, damaging homes, vehicles and a school. The two funnels formed off the coast near Marsala before moving inland towards Trapani, hitting the town of Petrosino along the way.

- South China Morning Post - China, The Hindu - International, ABC News Australia, Al Jazeera - Middle East, The Guardian - Australia, 2 hours ago: Russian attacks kill 17 in Ukraine after Trump strikes diesel deal with Putin.
Russian strikes killed at least 17 people in Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia region, Ukrainian officials said on Saturday, a day after US President Donald Trump announced a deal to buy Russian diesel that Kyiv warned would help bankroll Moscow’s war in Ukraine. Three children were among those killed when Russian aerial bombs hit residential buildings in Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine’s State Emergency Service said on Saturday. At least 18 people were wounded in the attack. Missiles also struck Kyiv in a daytime...

Police on Saturday said they detained 76 people across Poland and checked nearly 50,000 schools nationwide as part of efforts to prevent further violence following two school attacks earlier in the week. Chinese military aircraft may already be using a new joint aviation facility in Laos, with satellite imagery showing twice as many K-8/JL-8-family trainer aircraft there as the Laotian air force is assessed to possess. Eight of the two-seat trainer and light-attack aircraft were visible at Ban Keun Airport in commercial satellite imagery taken on September 30, according to Reuters, which first reported the images. South Asia - bottom line: Trump sows doubt on plan to livestream US military execution.
- Dawn (Pakistan), South China Morning Post - China, 8 hours ago: Trump sows doubt on plan to livestream US military execution.
US President Donald Trump has cast doubt on whether authorities will livestream the firing squad execution of the perpetrator of a deadly attack on American soldiers, a plan that has drawn broad and bipartisan condemnation, it emerged on Saturday. Nidal Hasan’s execution — scheduled for December 3 at Fort Hood, Texas, where he gunned down 13 people in 2009 — is set to be the first by a US military firing squad since 1945.
- Dawn (Pakistan), one hour ago: 10 terrorists killed during CTD operation in Barkhan, says Balochistan govt.
QUETTA: Ten terrorists were killed in a targeted intelligence-based operation conducted by the Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) in Balochistan’s Barkhan district, the Home Department said on Saturday. An aide in the Home Department, Babar Yousafzai, said: “During an intense gun battle, 10 armed terrorists were killed and two CTD officials were injured.” The CTD had conducted a targeted operation after receiving credible information about the presence of terrorists belonging to the Indian proxy, Fitna al Hindustan, in the area, according to Yousafzai.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 5 hours ago: Pakistan reaffirms commitment to Saudi security at UN Security Council.
UNITED NATIONS: Pakistan has reaffirmed its commitment to Saudi Arabia’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and security at the United Nations Security Council (UNSC), declaring that it would stand “shoulder to shoulder” with the kingdom in the face of continued Houthi attacks.
- The Hindu - International, 21 hours ago: Saudi authorities say three killed in Houthi-claimed attacks on Riyadh airport.
The attacks on October 8 were the deadliest in Saudi Arabia since the kingdom and allied forces in neighbouring Yemen launched a major military offensive against Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels last weekend

A luxurious estate in La Cañada Flintridge was recently sold for $8.5 million, attracting numerous potential buyers. The property includes a custom five-passenger garden railway that enhances its unique appeal and charm. Additionally, the house consists of six bedrooms, eight bathrooms, and a gourmet kitchen perfect for entertaining. Extensive outdoor features include a swimming pool, vegetable garden, and manicured landscapes recognized with multiple awards.

- Times of India - Top Stories, 6 hours ago: 'Send male officers forward’: Dipke tells women cops aboard flight before detention.
CJP convenor Abhijeet Dipke was detained at Delhi airport just before the planned Jantar Mantar protest. Dipke challenged police actions and demanded to speak with male officers during the detention. Security was heightened across Delhi due to the anticipated protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Other CJP leaders and a YouTuber were also reportedly detained ahead of the demonstration. Police cited law-and-order concerns for denying permission for the mobilization.
